title: Platform engineering (example)

role.summary: Keeps the billing service running: backups and restores, the storage server, and onboarding new developers.
role.context: A team of three; one person is on call each week.

stakeholders.name: Head of platform
stakeholders.relationship: Owns the platform and approves changes

tasks.name: Restore the billing database from backup
tasks.why_priority: The worst day; must be right first time

tasks.name: Set up the billing service on your laptop
tasks.why_priority: Every new developer needs it in week one

tasks.name: Replace a failed disk in the storage server
When the nightly backup job fails

processes.name: Restore the billing database from backup
processes.summary: Bring the billing database back from last night's backup without touching the live database.
processes.trigger: The billing database is lost or corrupted
prerequisites: Read access to the backup bucket
processes.rollback: Set DB_NAME back to billing, restart the service, and keep billing_restore until the incident is closed.
processes.escalation: Call the on-call DBA after 30 minutes or at the first data mismatch. Tell the head of platform if customers are affected.

people.involvement: Takes over if the restore fails

steps.title: Open an incident and tell the team
steps.detail: Post in the incidents channel: what broke, when, and that you are restoring.
steps.why: Others stop changing data and know who is in charge.

steps.title: Stop the billing service
steps.why: Nothing writes to the database while you restore.

steps.title: Find the latest good backup
steps.command: aws s3 ls s3://<BACKUP_BUCKET>/billing/ | sort | tail -n 3
steps.expected: Three dated .dump files; the newest is from last night

steps.title: Restore into a new database
steps.why: Restoring over the live database destroys the evidence and cannot be undone.

steps.title: Check the restored data
steps.branch_question: Does the newest invoice look right?

steps.title: Switch the app to the restored database
Start the service and watch the logs
steps.command: sudo systemctl start billing && journalctl -u billing -f
steps.expected: "Listening on :8080" and no errors for 5 minutes
steps.check: Open the billing page and find last night's newest invoice

steps.title: Stop and escalate
steps.detail: Leave the service stopped, keep billing_restore, and call the on-call DBA with what you saw.

rules.text: Never restore over the live database; always restore into a new one first.
rules.why: The live copy is the evidence and the fallback.

rules.text: Keep the broken database for 7 days for investigation.
rules.why: Summarised from "we keep it for a week or so".

scenarios.situation: The restore finished, but the newest invoice is from three days ago.
scenarios.question: What do you do?
options: Stop, keep the restored copy and call the on-call DBA
scenarios.explanation: Step 5: if the data does not look right, stop and escalate; never switch to a copy you cannot trust.

processes.name: Set up the billing service on your laptop
processes.summary: Get the billing service running locally with its tests passing, ready for your first change.
processes.trigger: Your first day, or a new laptop

steps.title: Clone the repository
steps.expected: A billing folder with package.json inside

steps.title: Start the local database
steps.expected: docker compose ps shows db as "healthy"

steps.title: Create your .env file
steps.detail: Fill in the values from the team password manager. Never commit .env.
steps.why: .env holds keys for the test payment provider.

rules.text: One branch per change, and a pull request reviewed by one other developer before merging.
rules.why: Every change gets a second pair of eyes.

rules.text: Run npm test before you push.
rules.why: CI takes 15 minutes; failing locally is faster.

rules.text: Never commit .env or real customer data.
rules.why: The repository is shared with contractors.

troubleshooting.fix: Stop it, or run PORT=3001 npm run dev

troubleshooting.cause: The database container is not running

troubleshooting.symptom: Tests fail on a fresh clone

scenarios.situation: Your change works, and you want to show a colleague quickly.
scenarios.question: How do you get it into main?
options: Open a pull request and get one review
Commit your .env so they can run it
scenarios.explanation: R-003 and R-005: every change goes through a reviewed pull request, and .env is never committed.

processes.name: Replace a failed disk in the storage server
processes.summary: Swap a failed disk in the storage server and check the RAID rebuild starts.
processes.trigger: The RAID controller reports a failed disk
ppe: ESD wrist strap, clipped to the rack
Safety glasses when the chassis is open
tools: Replacement disk, same model and size
Anti-static bag for the failed disk
prerequisites: The controller shows the disk as "Failed"

people.involvement: Watches the controller and confirms the slot

steps.title: Put on the ESD strap and clip it to the rack
steps.why: Static can kill the new disk or the backplane.

steps.title: Confirm the failed slot
steps.detail: Match the amber LED on the front with the slot number the controller reports.
steps.check: The second engineer reads the same slot number back to you

steps.title: Pull the caddy and swap the disk
steps.check: The new disk sits flat in the caddy

steps.title: Insert the caddy until it clicks
steps.check: The slot LED blinks green within 30 seconds

steps.title: Check the rebuild has started
steps.check: The controller shows "Rebuilding" for the slot

steps.title: Bag and label the failed disk
steps.detail: Write the date and slot on the bag; it goes to secure destruction, never the bin.

rules.text: Never pull a disk whose LED is green.
rules.why: Pulling a healthy disk during a degraded state loses the array.

scenarios.situation: Two slots show amber, but the controller reports only slot 3 as failed.
scenarios.question: Which disk do you pull?
options: Slot 3 only, after the second engineer confirms it
scenarios.explanation: Step 2: the slot is confirmed by two people against the controller before anything is pulled.

processes.name: When the nightly backup job fails
processes.summary: What to do when the backup alert fires, by what the job log says.
processes.trigger: The "backup failed" alert in the morning
processes.escalation: If the backup has failed two nights in a row, tell the head of platform before 10:00.

steps.title: Read the job log
steps.expected: The last lines say why the job stopped

troubleshooting.symptom: Job log: "No space left on device"
troubleshooting.fix: Delete dumps older than 14 days, then re-run: sudo systemctl start backup.service

troubleshooting.cause: The database restarted during the backup window

troubleshooting.symptom: The job did not run at all
troubleshooting.cause: The timer was disabled by a server update
troubleshooting.fix: sudo systemctl enable --now backup.timer, then run the job once
Ask the head of platform to update the secret; never paste keys into the job file

scenarios.situation: The upload fails and a colleague sends you the new bucket key in chat.
scenarios.question: What do you do?
options: Paste it into the job file
Ask the head of platform to update the secret properly, and tell the colleague to rotate it
scenarios.explanation: T-007: keys go through the secret store only; a key shared in chat must be rotated.
